   - Flag anything you could NOT pin down as an OPEN QUESTION with what you tried.
2. Differential test cases: one file per case at /workspace/dev/cases/<AREA>/<nn>-<slug>.txt containing the RAW bytes of the --a value (a trailing newline in the file IS part of the value; omit it if the value has none). Aim for 40-90 well-chosen cases in your area: normal, boundary, and adversarial. These will be replayed against both implementations byte-for-byte, so favor cases that discriminate between plausible implementations.
   Write case files with node/fs (or printf) so the bytes are exact. Verify each case actually runs the way you expect before keeping it. Do NOT keep a case whose observed behavior you did not record in the spec.

Your final message must be a compact summary of the RULES you established (not a list of files) — the most surprising/non-obvious findings first, at most 60 lines. Another engineer will implement from your spec file, but your summary is what the orchestrator reads.


AREA: command-line argument handling and failure modes.

## 1. Exit codes (complete set)

| situation | exit code | stream used |
|---|---|---|
| success | 0 | stdout |
| `-h` / `--help` (or any accepted abbreviation) | 0 | stdout |
| any argparse error | 2 | stderr |
| uncaught Python exception (bad YAML) | 1 | stderr |

There is **no** case that writes to both stdout and stderr.

## 2. `--help` / `-h` output (stdout, exit 0)

Exact bytes (verified with `od -c`; 99 bytes):

```
usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A<NL>
<NL>
options:<NL>
<SP><SP>-h, --help<SP><SP>show this help message and exit<NL>
<SP><SP>--a A<NL>
```

as one JSON string:

```
"usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A\n"
```

Details / rules:
* Heading is `options:` (Python >= 3.10), **not** `optional arguments:`.
* Blank line between the usage line and `options:`. No trailing blank line at the end.
* `  --a A` has **no** trailing spaces and no help text.
* Help column: `"  " + "-h, --help"` is 12 chars, then exactly 2 spaces -> help text starts
  at 0-based column 14. (argparse `help_position = min(action_max_length+2, 24)`.)

### 2.1 Program name
`prog` = `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])`. Verified: copying the binary to
`/workspace/tmp/zz-renamed` yields `usage: zz-renamed [-h] --a A`; invoking as

by that name).

### 2.2 Terminal width dependence (OPEN / environment)
Help & usage wrap at `COLUMNS-2`; with no `COLUMNS` and a non-tty stdout the fallback is
80 (=> width 78) and nothing wraps. Verified:
* `COLUMNS=200` -> identical to default.
* `COLUMNS=20` -> `"usage: test9_executable\n       [-h] --a A\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help\n    show this help\n    message and\n    exit\n  --a A\n"`

* `COLUMNS=1`  -> `"usage: test9_executable\n       [-h]\n       --a\n       A\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help\n    show this\n    help\n    message and\n    exit\n  --a A\n"`

A JS implementation may assume width 78 / no wrapping unless the harness sets `COLUMNS`.

## 3. argparse error output shape

Every argparse error is exactly two lines on **stderr**, exit code **2**:

```
usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A<NL>
test9_executable: error: <MESSAGE><NL>
```

i.e. `"usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A\ntest9_executable: error: " + MESSAGE + "\n"`.

Observed `<MESSAGE>` values:

| message | trigger |
|---|---|
| `the following arguments are required: --a` | `--a` never supplied |
| `argument --a: expected one argument` | `--a` present but the next token is classified as an option (or absent) |
| `unrecognized arguments: <t1> <t2> ...` | leftover tokens, `' '.join(extras)` |
| `ambiguous option: <tok> could match --help, --a` | a `--`-prefixed token whose prefix matches >1 long option |
| `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<x>'` | `-h`/`--help` given an explicit `=`-value or a `-`-leading tail |

Verified by construction:

1. **Pre-scan of the whole argv** classifies every token. An *ambiguous option* is raised

`["-h"]`, `["-h","-h"]`, `["--b","-h"]`, `["extra","-h"]`, `["-h","--b"]`, `["--A","-h"]`,

  empty value -> `"--- null\n...\n\n"`.
  (This is PyYAML's `open_ended` behaviour: an "open ended" plain/`null` document root gets
  `...` before the stream ends.) A quoted scalar root does **not**:
  `-١٢` -> `"--- \"-\\u0661\\u0662\"\n\n"` (no `...`).
* `stderr` empty.
* Values `""`, `" "`, `"\n"`, `"\n\n"`, `"# c only"`, `"--- "` all -> `"--- null\n...\n\n"`.
* Duplicate mapping keys are allowed, **last wins**: `"a: 1\na: 2"` -> `"---\na: 2\n\n"`.
* An anchor referenced by an alias is re-emitted as `&id001`/`*id001`:
  `"&x {a: 1, b: *x}"` -> `"--- &id001\na: 1\nb: *id001\n\n"`.
* A leading U+FEFF BOM is stripped by the reader; a BOM later in the stream becomes data:
  `"a: 1\n﻿b: 2"` -> `"---\na: 1\n\"\\uFEFFb\": 2\n\n"`.

## 7. Uncaught-exception (bad YAML) failure mode

* **stdout is completely empty** — `print` never runs because the exception is raised in the
  same statement. Nothing is flushed. Verified for every case in section 10.
* **exit code 1.**
* Everything goes to **stderr**, in this layout:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):<NL>
<SP><SP>File "test9.py", line 8, in <module><NL>
<SP><SP>File "yaml/__init__.py", line 125, in safe_load<NL>
... more frames ...<NL>
<EXCEPTION-TYPE>: <str(exception)><NL>
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test9' due to unhandled exception!<NL>
```

Rules:
* **No source-code lines** in the traceback — PyInstaller strips them, so each frame is a
  single `  File "...", line N, in NAME` line with exactly 2 leading spaces. (A normal
  CPython traceback would add a 4-space-indented source line per frame; this binary never does.)
* The first frame is always `  File "test9.py", line 8, in <module>` (line 8 of the *compiled*
  source, which has blank lines the quoted snippet above doesn't).
* Frame paths are relative POSIX paths (`yaml/scanner.py`, not absolute).
* `str(exception)` can be multi-line (see 7.1) — everything up to the `[PYI-...]` line.
* **`<pid>` in the `[PYI-...]` line is the process id and therefore NOT reproducible.**
  Verified: consecutive runs gave `PYI-2819`, `PYI-2824`, `PYI-2828`. Any differential
  comparison must normalise `\[PYI-\d+:ERROR\]`. A JS reimplementation should emit
  `[PYI-<its own pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test9' due to unhandled exception!`.
* Trailing newline after the `[PYI-...]` line is present.

### 7.1 `str(exception)` layout for `yaml.error.MarkedYAMLError` subclasses

Joined with `\n` from these parts, each omitted when absent:

1. `context`            (e.g. `while scanning a quoted scalar`)
2. `str(context_mark)`  — omitted when it is at the same name/line/column as `problem_mark`
3. `problem`            (e.g. `found unexpected end of stream`)
4. `str(problem_mark)`
5. `note`               (never observed to be present in this corpus)

`str(mark)` is:

```
<SP><SP>in "<unicode string>", line L, column C:<NL>
<SP><SP><SP><SP>[head]<line-fragment>[tail]<NL>
<caret-indent>^
```

* Stream name is the literal `<unicode string>` (because the input is a `str`).
* `L`, `C` are **1-based**, counted in **Unicode code points** (not UTF-16 units, not bytes).
  Verified: `😀😀: @x` -> `line 1, column 5` (2 emoji + `:` + `<SP>` = 4 code points before);
  `ααααα: @x` -> `column 8`.
* Line breaks recognised by the reader/scanner: `\n`, `\r`, `\0`, U+0085 (NEL),
  U+2028 (LS), U+2029 (PS). Verified: `a: 1<CR>@x`, `a: 1<U+0085>@x`, `a: 1<U+2028>@x`
  all report `line 2, column 1`.
* Snippet (`Mark.get_snippet(indent=4, max_length=75)`), with `pointer` = the 0-based
  code-point offset of the mark and `bol`/`eol` the enclosing line boundaries:
  * `before = pointer - bol` (code points on the line before the mark).
    If `before <= 36`: `head = ""`, keep all of them.
    If `before >= 37`: `head = "<SP>...<SP>"` (5 chars: space, 3 dots, space) and keep only
    the **last 32** code points before the mark.
  * `after = eol - pointer` (code points from the mark to end of line).
    If `after <= 36`: `tail = ""`, keep all of them.
    If `after >= 37`: keep only the **first 32** and append `tail = "<SP>...<SP>"`
    (note the **trailing space before the newline**).
  * snippet line = `"    " + head + kept + tail`.
  * caret line  = `" " * (4 + len(head) + (pointer - start)) + "^"` where `pointer - start`
    is 32 when head was applied, `before` otherwise. **No trailing spaces on the caret line.**
  * Threshold pinned exactly: the CPython source condition is `> max_length/2 - 1` = `> 36.5`.
    Verified with `before` = 33/36/37/38/40/60 and `after` = 30/34/35/36/37/40 — the
    truncation appears first at 37 in both directions (cases 81-85).
  * **The snippet is copied verbatim, including literal TABs** (so the caret does not line
    up visually): `a:<TAB>b: 1` -> snippet `    a:<TAB>b: 1`, caret line `      ^`
    (4 + 2 = 6 spaces).

### 7.2 `str(exception)` layout for `yaml.reader.ReaderError`

Two lines, and **no snippet / no caret**:

```
unacceptable character #x<hhhh>: special characters are not allowed<NL>
<SP><SP>in "<unicode string>", position P<NL>
```

* `<hhhh>` is `%04x` — lowercase, zero-padded to at least 4 digits (`#x0001`, `#x007f`,
  `#x0084`, `#xfffe`).
* `P` is the **0-based code-point index** of the offending character (`😀😀x\x01` -> `position 3`).
* Printable set (PyYAML `NON_PRINTABLE`): allowed are `\x09 \x0A \x0D`, `\x20-\x7E`,
  `\x85`, `\xA0-퟿`, `-�`, `\U00010000-\U0010FFFF`.
  Verified: `\x7f`, `\x84`, `\x86`, `\x9f`, `\xfffe` rejected; `\x7e`, `\x85` (a line break),
  `\xa0`, `�` accepted.
* This error fires in `Reader.__init__`, i.e. **before any scanning**, so it pre-empts every
  scanner/parser error in the same input.

| `!!int ""` | `IndexError: string index out of range` |
| `!!timestamp xyz` | `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'groupdict'` |

## 9. OPEN QUESTIONS / not pinned down

1. **`[PYI-<pid>:ERROR]` line** — the number is the OS pid, unreproducible by construction.
   Not resolvable; must be normalised by the differential harness.
2. **Traceback frame lists** are reproduced in section 10 for the 54 error cases in the
   corpus, but they are *derived from PyYAML's internal call graph*. A JS implementation must
   hard-code the frame list per error site; there is no rule to derive it. Any error site not
   in the corpus is unknown.
3. **Invalid UTF-8 in argv** — CPython decodes argv with `surrogateescape`, so a raw `0xFF`
   byte becomes U+DCFF and produces
   `yaml.reader.ReaderError: unacceptable character #xdcff: special characters are not allowed`
   at the right position. Only spot-checked with one byte (`--a "a: \xff"`); the general
   surrogateescape mapping (`0x80-0xFF` -> `U+DC80-U+DCFF`) was not exhaustively verified,
   and the differential harness (Node `spawnSync` with a JS string) cannot produce such argv.
4. **`note` field of `MarkedYAMLError`** — never observed non-`None`; the extra trailing line
   it would produce is untested. Probed ~40 error inputs (scanner/parser/composer/constructor)
   without hitting one.
5. **Terminal-width wrapping** of help/usage depends on `COLUMNS`; only the values 1, 15, 20,
   200 and unset were probed. The general `HelpFormatter` wrapping algorithm was not derived.
6. `--a` values large enough to exceed `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` / `ARG_MAX` were not probed.

Spec: `/workspace/dev/spec/cli-and-errors.md` — 90 cases in `/workspace/dev/cases/cli-and-errors/` (all re-verified deterministic, byte-for-byte).

RULES ESTABLISHED (most surprising first)

1. `[PYI-<n>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test9' due to unhandled exception!` is appended to stderr after every Python traceback — `<n>` is the **PID**, so it is not reproducible. Harness must normalise `\[PYI-\d+:ERROR\]`.
2. Tracebacks contain **no source-code lines** (PyInstaller strips them). Each frame is exactly `  File "yaml/scanner.py", line N, in fn`; first frame is always `  File "test9.py", line 8, in <module>`. Frame lists are per-error-site and must be hard-coded (recorded for all 54 error cases).
3. `["--a","-5"]` works but `["--a","-x"]` fails. The negative-number escape hatch is Python `re` `^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$` where `\d` is **Unicode Nd**: `-١٢`(U+0661/2), `-５`(U+FF15), `-۱.۲` are accepted as values; `-²`(No), `-一`, `-1e5`, `-1.`, `-1_0` are rejected with `argument --a: expected one argument`.
4. Second escape hatch: a value containing an **ASCII 0x20 space** is always a value (`-x y`, `- a`, `- ` OK). NBSP and TAB do not count (`-<NBSP>5`, `-<TAB>` → error).
5. `-h ` (trailing space) still errors, because the short-prefix check (`V[:2]=="-h"`) runs *before* the space check. Full 9-step classification order is in spec §5.
6. `["--a","--","x"]` → `expected one argument`. `--` cannot be skipped to reach an optional's value (argparse strips `-*` from the nargs pattern of optionals → pattern is `(A)`).
7. An unconsumed `--` **stays in extras**: `["--a","1","--"]` → `unrecognized arguments: --`; `["--a","1","--","x","--"]` → `unrecognized arguments: -- x --`.
8. Missing `--a` **beats** unknown options: `["--b"]`, `["-a"]`, `["-x"]`, `["-"]`, `["--"]`, `["--A"]` all give `the following arguments are required: --a` — the bad token is never named. `unrecognized arguments:` is only reachable once `--a` has a value.
9. `-h` wins over *every* other error wherever it sits in argv (`["--b","-h"]`, `["extra","-h"]`, `["--x=1","-h"]` → help, rc 0) — EXCEPT (a) `ambiguous option` which is raised in the whole-argv pre-scan (`["-h","--=x"]` → rc 2), and (b) errors from options consumed earlier (`["-h=1","-h"]`, `["--a","-h","1"]` → rc 2).
10. `--=x` / `--=` → `ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --a` (order = registration order, long options only).
11. `-hh`, `-h1`, `-hx` → help (single-dash tail re-parsed). `-h=1`, `--help=1`, `--h=1`, `-h-`, `-h--`, `--help=` → `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<x>'` (`''` for `--help=`). Rule: tail accepted iff not introduced by `=` and its first char isn't `-`.
12. Abbreviation: `--h`/`--he`/`--hel` → help. `--A`, `--aa`, `--a1`, `---` are unknown.
13. Exit codes: 0 success/help, **2** argparse, **1** uncaught exception. Errors are always exactly `"usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A\n" + "test9_executable: error: " + MSG + "\n"` on stderr; help is on stdout. No run ever writes both streams.
14. `--help` stdout is exactly `"usage: test9_executable [-h] --a A\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A\n"` (heading `options:`, help column 14, no trailing blank line). `prog` = basename(argv[0]) — hard-code `test9_executable`. `COLUMNS` re-wraps usage+help (values 1/15/20 recorded); the `error:` line itself never wraps.
15. On a YAML error **stdout is completely empty** — nothing is flushed, because `print` is in the same statement. Normal output ends with **two** `\n` (`yaml.dump` + `print`), and a **scalar/`null` root additionally emits `...`**: `x` → `"--- x\n...\n\n"`, `""`/`" "`/`"\n"`/`"# c"`/`"--- "` → `"--- null\n...\n\n"`. A *quoted* scalar root does not get `...`.
16. `MarkedYAMLError.__str__` = `\n`-join of [context, str(context_mark), problem, str(problem_mark), note], with `context_mark` **omitted when it has the same line/column as `problem_mark`**. `note` was never observed non-None.
17. Mark block = `  in "<unicode string>", line L, column C:` + snippet + caret. L/C are 1-based **code points** (`😀😀: @x` → column 5). Line breaks include `\n \r \0 U+0085 U+2028 U+2029`.
18. Snippet truncation (`indent=4, max_length=75`, threshold `>36.5`): if >36 code points precede the mark on its line, prepend `<SP>...<SP>` and keep only the last **32**; if >36 follow, keep the first **32** and append `<SP>...<SP>` (**trailing space before the newline**). Caret leading spaces = `4 + (head ? 37 : before)`. Max snippet line = 78. Pinned with before/after = 36 vs 37. Snippet copies literal TABs, so the caret visually misaligns.
19. `ReaderError` has a *different* shape — no snippet, no caret: `unacceptable character #x%04x: special characters are not allowed\n  in "<unicode string>", position P` with `P` a **0-based code-point index**, hex lowercase 4-wide. Fires in `Reader.__init__`, pre-empting all scanner/parser errors. Rejected: `\x7f`, `\x84`, `\x86`, `\x9f`, `\xfffe`; allowed: `\x7e`, `\x85`, `\xa0`, `\xfffd`. Invalid UTF-8 argv bytes surface via surrogateescape as `#xdcff`.
20. Some `!!`-tagged scalars escape as raw Python exceptions with **no mark block at all**: `!!int abc`→`ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'`; `!!float xyz`→`ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'xyz'`; `!!bool xyz`→`KeyError: 'xyz'`; `!!int ""`→`IndexError: string index out of range`; `!!timestamp xyz`→`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'groupdict'`.
21. Not errors (rc 0): duplicate mapping keys (**last wins**), `? b` explicit key, invalid escape `"a\qb"` (passes through), `%TAG ! x`, leading BOM (stripped; mid-stream BOM becomes data), `&x {a: 1, b: *x}` → re-emitted as `&id001`/`*id001`.
22. `--a=v` splits on the **first** `=` only (`--a=1=2` → value `1=2`); `--a=` and `--a ""` are identical (→ `null`); repeated `--a` → **last wins**.

OPEN QUESTIONS: PYI pid line (unfixable); per-error-site traceback frame lists have no derivable rule (only the 54 corpus sites are known); `note` field never triggered; general `COLUMNS` wrapping algorithm not derived; full surrogateescape mapping only spot-checked; ARG_MAX limits unprobed.
